guarantees.claim: ready_o is directly driven by sp_ready after a cast to sp2v_e type.
ctr_we is directly driven by sp_ctr_we after a cast to sp2v_e type.
alert_o is the bitwise OR reduction of all bits of mr_alert.

assumptions.claim: sp_ready value stays within the representable range of sp2v_e type (no overflow/truncation).
assumptions.risk: Truncated or corrupted sp_ready may cause ready_o to mis-signal, leading to handshake deadlock or data corruption.

assumptions.claim: sp_ctr_we value stays within the representable range of sp2v_e type.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect ctr_we could enable unintended counter writes, corrupting AES CTR internal state.

assumptions.claim: mr_alert bits are driven to zero when no alert condition exists; only legitimate alert sources may assert them.
assumptions.risk: Spurious assertion of mr_alert bits would cause false alert_o trigger, potentially activating security error responses unnecessarily.

uncertain_points.claim: The width of sp2v_e and the width of sp_ready/sp_ctr_we are not defined locally. A mismatch would cause silent truncation during the cast.
uncertain_points.risk: ready_o or ctr_we could incorrectly reflect only a subset of sp_ready, leading to handshake corruption or unintended write strobes.

uncertain_points.claim: The significance of individual mr_alert bits (which error source each bit represents) is not defined here.
uncertain_points.risk: A missing or mis-assigned alert bit could hide a critical fault condition from the security alert handler.
